parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Measure a capability, not a prototype count
parts.body:
An AI maturity report should answer whether the organization can repeatedly select worthwhile uses, deliver them safely, measure results, and change course. Count deployed systems, but do not confuse volume with maturity. Organize evidence around value, adoption, delivery, reliability, governance, incidents, talent, and pipeline. NIST's Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage functions are a useful way to test whether controls span the lifecycle.

Give every metric an owner, definition, denominator, source, cadence, and action threshold. 'Adoption' could mean active eligible staff using a tool in an intended workflow, rather than all accounts ever created. 'Value realized' needs an agreed baseline and net cost. 'Evaluation current' needs a meaningful expiry or change trigger, especially when a vendor changes a model. A traffic-light color without this metadata invites false confidence.

Report both leading and outcome signals. Training completion can indicate readiness but says little about competent use. A blind quality sample and a business outcome give stronger evidence. Note coverage: if only three of twenty systems have measured outcomes, say so.

example.title: Six-measure operating scorecard
example.body: Illustrative claims assistant, one month; thresholds are locally proposed. Value: net minutes saved per eligible case, baseline 0, current 1.8 across 1,000 of 1,200 cases measured, threshold at least 2; finance owner, medium confidence, recalculate rework cost. Adoption: active eligible adjusters / 100, baseline 40/100, current 60/100, threshold at least 55/100; claims owner, complete roster, continue training. Quality: drafts meeting rubric / reviewed drafts, baseline 94/100, current 88/100, threshold at least 93/100; evaluation lead, stratified sample but wide uncertainty, hold expansion and investigate errors. Risk: open severe incidents / all deployed uses, baseline 0/1, current 0/1, threshold 0; CISO, reporting route tested but low event-detection confidence, audit samples. Delivery: release gates passed on time / planned gates, baseline 2/3, current 3/4, threshold at least 3/4; program lead, complete gate log, clear overdue item. Capability: trained reviewers passing a scenario check / 100 eligible, baseline 45/100, current 72/100, threshold 80/100; workforce lead, 90 responses received, schedule targeted practice. Rising adoption does not override the failed quality gate.

exercise.title: Define six measures
exercise.body: Write one measure each for value, adoption, quality, risk, delivery, and capability. Give numerator, denominator, owner, source, cadence, and decision threshold. Flag any measure that has no baseline.

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Read conflicting signals
parts.body:
A mature report does not force a single green score when indicators disagree. Suppose monthly users rise 40% while manual corrections and escalations double. Check whether case mix, volume, review rules, or model behavior changed. Compare rates using eligible cases and a stable definition. Inspect severity and affected groups, not only the total correction count. Rising corrections might reflect better detection, worse output, or both.

Set a temporary decision while the investigation runs. The product owner may hold wider rollout, increase human review, or revert a model version. Assign an investigation lead, sample plan, deadline, and condition for resuming growth. Keep the distinction between a signal and a proven cause.

A small chart can show adoption, correction rate, and cost per completed case across the same periods. Use separate axes or small aligned charts with clearly labeled units; a single composite maturity score hides the tradeoff. Annotate a release or policy change so a reader can investigate its effect rather than assume causation.

example.title: A hold decision from conflicting signals
example.body: In the six-measure scorecard, adoption rises from 40/100 to 60/100 but reviewed quality falls from 94/100 to 88/100, below the 93/100 release floor. The claims VP holds expansion for two weeks and keeps human review in place. The evaluation lead samples cases by type and severity and checks whether the rubric or case mix changed; finance recalculates net minutes after correction. Expansion resumes only after a fresh representative sample clears the agreed quality floor and unit value is positive. These thresholds and figures are illustrative.

exercise.title: Diagnose the false positive
exercise.body: Draft a four-line executive note for rising users and doubled corrections. State observed facts, two plausible explanations, immediate action, evidence owner, and date. Sketch a chart showing the rates with denominators.

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Make governance coverage visible
parts.body:
Report the share of material AI systems with a named business owner, current inventory record, documented purpose, evaluation appropriate to the use, incident route, and next review date. A missing record is itself a coverage gap. Show how long exceptions remain open and which authority can accept or close them. A reported zero incidents is weak evidence if staff have no way to recognize or report one.

Geography belongs in the inventory. For EU uses, record the provider or deployer role, classification assessment, applicable obligations, and counsel's review date. For Canadian data, record the privacy regime and purpose assessment. Legal requirements and their timing may change; the report should link to the current review rather than freeze a generic claim of compliance.

Avoid reward systems that encourage hiding risk. If a team is measured only on 'percent green,' it may narrow the inventory or postpone testing. Pair coverage with independent sampling, overdue exceptions, and incident learning. The board should see who owns remediation and when a gap may change deployment status.

example.title: Coverage with its denominator
example.body: Of 18 material systems in the inventory, 16 have current evaluations, 15 have a tested incident route, and two EU uses await updated classification review. One release remains held. This describes management's control coverage, not legal compliance.

exercise.title: Audit a dashboard
exercise.body: Given 20 registered uses and five unregistered experiments, recalculate evaluation coverage using both denominators. Explain why the difference matters. Add a column for Canadian or EU assessment owner where relevant.

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Turn the scorecard into a decision cadence
parts.body:
Different audiences need different detail. A product owner reviews quality, adoption, incidents, and unit cost frequently enough to act. The executive committee examines investment, capability bottlenecks, and exceptions monthly or quarterly. The board sees material exposure, realized value, and choices requiring oversight. Tie every red or amber measure to an action, owner, and date; tie every green one to its evidence and coverage.

Publish definitions with the report and preserve prior snapshots. When a metric changes, show the old and new methods for one period rather than drawing a seamless trend across incompatible data. If you expand the inventory, a falling coverage percentage may represent improved discovery. Explain it instead of editing the earlier denominator.

End a review with explicit portfolio moves: scale, correct, narrow, pause, or retire. Maturity is visible in those decisions and in the evidence behind them. A polished dashboard that never changes funding or controls has become decoration.

example.title: A quarterly decision
example.body: Invoice assistant shows verified time savings, stable quality, and declining cost, so expand to one additional team. Recruiting screen shows unresolved disparate error rates, so hold expansion and commission a reviewed evaluation. Both decisions have owners and return dates.

exercise.title: Run the review
exercise.body: Create a one-page scorecard with six measures and two conflicting signals. Ask a peer acting as CFO or CISO to recommend an investment or control change. Record the decision, owner, evidence gap, and next review.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage
